decision: The exact subject is accepted for the Owner/web-flow signature. The single blocking defect of the first round (NW02-R1: approval.proposal_path / proposal_sha256 named NextWindowPlanV2Window12Cycle.md, which is not the proposal for approval f92cd46e) is repaired and the repair was verified independently, not taken on the sidecar's word: this session fetched pull request 164 from the GitHub REST API itself and the response body is 6461 bytes whose sha256 is b340f46d1aeb64b338651504cf42b67ef643c56508517a6fca0efd49a40b2827, byte-identical under cmp(1) to the archived OwnerApprovalProposalPR164.md the subject now pins, with no trailing newline added and nothing appended - so the CAPTURED_NOT_AUTHORED claim is established, not merely asserted. Every item the first round had already passed was recomputed here from primary sources rather than carried over. The subject accepts nothing beyond the fixed window it describes: it does not renew accepted_binding, append Root or Status, register root7, reserve budget, create a GA, or authorize execution. It remains CANDIDATE_FOR_OWNER_SIGNATURE_NOT_LIVE until the Owner merge that publishes it. The prepared transaction NW02Applied.sql is NOT accepted by this document and is separately rejected in the store acceptance issued alongside it.

findings.difference_from_nw01_recorded_not_charge: NW-01's proposal was inside the tree of the approval merge itself (cbe898d3); this one is not - OwnerApprovalProposalPR164.md was first committed at 6816597, after the approval. It will be in the tree of the merge that carries the Owner signature over this subject, which is the merge that matters for a path pin, so the pin resolves when it is read. Recorded as a difference in kind, not as a defect.
how_this_session_verified_it_rather_than: Fetched GET /repos/tdoljyj/cross-memory-system/pulls/164 directly over the agent proxy with this session's own credentials (HTTP 200), not via the repository artifact and not via the MCP wrapper alone.
Extracted the response's body field and wrote it to a scratch file: 6461 bytes, sha256 b340f46d1aeb64b338651504cf42b67ef643c56508517a6fca0efd49a40b2827.
cmp(1) of that scratch file against the committed OwnerApprovalProposalPR164.md reported no difference: the archive is the API body verbatim.
The body contains no CRLF, so the digest is not an artifact of line-ending normalization: the CRLF-normalized form has the same length and the same digest.

od(1) on the last bytes of the archived file shows it ends at the final ')' / '_' of the PR body with no trailing LF appended, which is what a verbatim capture looks like and what an edited or re-authored Markdown file would almost certainly not look like.

No post-hoc prose was mixed in: since the bytes are bit-for-bit the API response, the set of inserted characters is empty by construction. CAPTURED_NOT_AUTHORED is therefore established, not merely claimed.

The PR body has not been edited since the approval: pull request 164 reports created_at 2026-09-13T05:24:12Z, merged_at 2026-09-13T05:45:14Z and updated_at 2026-09-13T05:45:14Z, i.e. updated_at equals merged_at, so nothing about the pull request changed after the merge that was the approval. (GitHub's GraphQL userContentEdits history is not reachable from this environment; this is the strongest available REST evidence and is recorded as such.)

why_the_pin_is_the_right_document: The M3 carrier states its own approval act as approval_action: OWNER_MERGES_CONTAINING_PULL_REQUEST_VIA_GITHUB_WEB_FLOW. What was put to the Owner at that act is the pull request, and the pull request's prose is its body. The archived body is therefore the proposal by role, independently of how well it is written.

Unlike the NW-01 lineage, the M3 package contains no in-tree prose proposal: the 6 files the approval merge added under bootstrap/next-window-m3/ are the approval candidate, an independent opinion, two note files and two scripts. There was no OwnerApprovalProposalM3.md to name. Naming the PR body is the only choice that names something that actually played the role.
The pin is content-addressed (path + sha256) exactly as NW-01's was, and the content is re-derivable from a primary source at any time, as this session just demonstrated.

A proposal that understates a downstream obligation is still the proposal; NW-01's proposal was likewise not gated on being correct. The defective sentence lives in a sidecar with authority_effect NONE that the subject does not pin, so it is outside the bytes the Owner signs. The primary ground for the pin, set out above, does not rest on it.

findings.refinement_this_round: Round 1 read this as 'the subject asserts conformance to a schema it categorically fails'. That reading is probably too strong. In the sibling subject family the same schema path appears as storage_candidate.schema_responsibility - a pointer to the schema that governs the ROOT SET, checked as such by scripts/phase2-qualification/control-root-registration/verify.py - not as a conformance claim about the document carrying it. Read that way, schema_sha256 names the schema of the trust-root set this binding belongs to, and no contradiction arises. The document does not say which reading is intended, and that ambiguity is the thing actually worth fixing upstream.
findings.summary: schema_sha256 87f094fa079034aa886d6c568730370a3264e106529b4bfd79bc3369f30b79e5 is the digest of protocol/continuity/v1/schemas/core/control-trust-root-set.schema.json ($id urn:clued:schema:control-trust-root-set:v1, title ControlTrustRootSet, object_type const ControlTrustRootSet, additionalProperties false, 20 required keys). The subject declares object_type AcceptedBindingContinuationWindow, lacks 15 of those 20 required keys and carries 16 keys the schema forbids. Re-measured this round; the same file also exists byte-identically at scripts/phase2-qualification/nonproduction-control-store/protocol-successor/control-trust-root-set.schema.json.
findings.why_not_a_rejection_ground_here: The value is inherited: the NW-01 subject carries it and this session read it live from clued_control.accepted_binding.schema_sha256, where it is identical. schema_sha256 is one of the nine columns the NW-02 transaction must leave untouched, so NW-02 has no authority to change it, and a subject naming a different schema would disagree with the row it describes. Carried upward to whoever owns the row's schema binding.
